co_crater_crag_of_north_quarry.blurb: Crater Crag is a compact face on the east side of the quarry cliffs at the top of North Table Mountain, just outside Golden. Eleven climbs mix sport, top-rope and a couple of trad lines, and the difficulty leans hard: a single easier line near 5.8, a few at 5.10, then a cluster in the 5.11s and a pair of 5.12s. Because it looks east, the wall goes into shade in the early afternoon, which makes it a decent pick on warm days. The walk up is short and follows a well-defined trail, with some loose gravel near the base.

_expect.name: Turtle Rock: A Crag for Kids

co_turtle_rock_a_crag_for_kids.blurb: Turtle Rock is a very small, turtle-shaped outcrop in Boulder Canyon, a short uphill walk from the road and out of sight of it. It was set up with beginners and children in mind: eleven short trad routes, mostly between 5.4 and 5.9, over a slab, cracks, an overhang and a dihedral, with a few bolts at the top anchors and on the slab. Everything else needs a small trad rack. Expect a quick visit rather than a full day, a steep, faint path to reach it, and some loose rock and debris up top.

co_cat_slab_annex.blurb: Cat Slab Annex fills a big dihedral just south of the Cat Slab in Clear Creek Canyon, west of Golden. Most of the eleven climbs are bolted sport lines, with one top-rope and one trad route, and the grades run from easy 5.6 up to several 5.11s. The left side of the corner holds the gentler routes, including a pair of two-pitch moderates that suit newer multi-pitch climbers, while the upper right is steeper and more overhanging and the lower right is loose. A practice anchor between two of the easy routes lets parties rehearse rope systems. The walk from the Tunnel 5 parking is brief.

co_conspiracy_crag_the.blurb: The Conspiracy Crag is a newer, high-standard sport wall above Clear Creek Canyon near Golden, perched several hundred feet over the creek. All eleven routes are bolted and under 100 feet, so one 60 m rope handles the lot. The grades are demanding: about half sit in the 5.11s, nearly as many in the 5.12s, and one reaches 5.13. The wall faces east to southeast, catching sun from morning to early afternoon with no shade trees, so it is poor in winter but can be a pleasant escape from summer heat. Reaching it takes roughly twenty minutes up a loose, cairned hillside.

co_physical_crag.blurb: Physical Crag is a remote, two-tier cliff west of Eldorado Canyon, on the hogback above the state park rather than in the canyon itself. Its eleven climbs are all traditional, with a few usable as top-ropes, and they sit in the 5.9 to 5.11 range. The stone is coarser and more lichen-covered than the canyon's usual rock, and the climbing is mostly short, technical face moves that can be runout or poorly protected. It faces west-southwest and gets afternoon sun. Expect about an hour of hiking, solitude, and a self-reliant day; bring extra webbing and rappel rings for the lower tier.

co_vanishing_point.blurb: Vanishing Point is one of about twenty crags in Upper Dream Canyon, a secluded pocket of climbing in the foothills near Boulder. It holds eleven routes, most of them bolted sport lines with a few gear routes, running from an approachable 5.8 or 5.9 through several 5.10s and 5.11s to a handful of 5.12s. The terrain is varied, with slabs, bulges, corners and arêtes, so it suits a mixed party that wants both moderate and harder climbs. The canyon can be tricky to find without someone to show you the way, so study the directions beforehand.
